227: Rabbi Yose started, "And you shall eat, and you shall be sated, and you shall bless the Lord your God for the good land that He has given you (Deuteronomy 8:10). If [we are] in the land of Israel, we bless. But from where [do we know it when we are] outside of the land? [As it seems] that, in this way, there is no need for it! Rather, when the Holy One, blessed be He, created the world, he divided the world, the inhabitable land on one side and the uninhabitable land on the other side. He divided the inhabitable land and centered the world around one point. And what was it? It was the holy land; the holy land is in the center of the world. And Jerusalem is in the center of the holy land, and the holy of holies is in the center of Jerusalem. And all the entire inhabitable land's good and all of its sustenance descends there from above. So there is no place in all the inhabitable land that is not sustained from there."

One who luxuriates at his table and delights in those foods ought to call to mind and to feel concern for the holiness of the Holy Land and for the Temple of the King that has been destroyed. In consideration of the sadness that one feels at one's table--in the midst of the joy and celebration [lit. drinking] there--the Holy Blessed One accounts it to one as if one has rebuilt His House and rebuilt all the ruins of the Temple. Happy is one's portion!
